title: Climbing: from the mountains to the city
text:
Climbing began as a way of reaching mountain tops {A}. For most of the twentieth century it remained an expensive pastime, {B}. Then indoor walls started to appear in big cities, and the sport became unrecognisable. Today a beginner can try it after work, in an ordinary sports centre, {C} the basic safety rules.

The simplest form is bouldering, in which climbers stay close to the ground and rely on thick mats rather than ropes. In lead climbing, by contrast, people go much higher, secured by a rope {D} as they rise. The third discipline is speed climbing, {E} on a standard route of fifteen metres.

In 2021 climbing made its Olympic debut in Tokyo, and many viewers discovered it at home on television. Coaches say that the sport develops not only strength and balance {F}. Perhaps that is why it attracts so many people who never considered themselves sporty.
